title: spec-dna.toml
description: The project configuration of spec-dna. spec-dna reads it as TOML. See docs/config.md.

spec-dna.description: The pinned spec-dna version. `check` does not run with a binary of another version.

profile.description: The profile of the project: the default severity of each diagnostic code. Default `standard`.

types.description: The document types of the project. A document of another type is an error (SD303), and `spec-dna new` does not accept it. Default: every type.

tests.description: Globs of the test files where `check` reads `covers: <doc-id>#<key>` tags. An empty list turns the tags off. Default: the usual test directories and file names of common stacks.

exclude.description: Repository path globs that are never documents (vendored or generated text). Links to them still resolve as files.

self-urls.description: URL prefixes that address this repository. A link under one of them resolves as a path from the repository root. `*` is one whole path segment, such as a branch.

install-source.description: The git source of spec-dna for `cargo install --git`, such as `file:///srv/git/spec-dna` or `ssh://git@host/team/spec-dna.git`. The message of a version mismatch uses it. Default: the public repository.

spec-dna-sha256.description: The SHA-256 sums of the release assets of the pin. A key is an asset name, `spec-dna-<version>-<target>`, with `.exe` for a Windows target. If the pin is the version of the binary, the binary also checks that each key is an asset of that version. Copy the table from `spec-dna-pin.toml` of the release.

roots.description: Directories of documents. A path belongs to the deepest root that contains it.

budgets.description: Size budgets in Unicode characters of body text, per document type.

growth.description: The number of characters that a document over its hard budget in the base can grow in one change. Growth up to this number gives a warning (SD703), not an error (SD702). Default 4000.

max-words.description: The maximum number of words in a requirement sentence. A longer sentence gives a warning. Default 30.

budget.description: The default character budget of `spec-dna context`. Default 8000.

conventions.description: For each type, pointers (`<doc-id or path>[#<anchor>]`) to the sections of project documents, or of Markdown files that are not documents (outside every root, or excluded), that state the conventions of the project for documents of that type. `context` serves them first when a target is a document of that type. `show --conventions <type>` prints them. A pointer that names nothing gives SD106.

repos.description: Aliases of other repositories for `<repo>:<namespace>/<slug>` references.

pattern.description: Literal text with exactly one `{n}` (one or more digits). `*` matches any text.

path.description: Directory relative to the repository root. Use `.` for the whole repository.

type.description: The type of every document in the root. With `mixed` (the default), the front matter of each document gives the type.

default-type.description: For mixed roots only: the type of a document that has no `type` field. Default `note`.

status.description: The status of a document that has the default type of the root and no `status` field.

exclude.description: Globs relative to the root that are not documents.

legacy-ids.description: Patterns that make aliases from the names of files, such as `ADR-{n}`.

legacy-keys.description: Patterns of requirement keys that spec-dna keeps as written, such as `R-{n}`.

status-map.description: Legacy status words, each with the status that it maps to, such as `released = "active"`. The target must be a status of the type of the root, or of any type in a mixed root.

required-sections.description: For each type, its required sections. The value is a list of headings (one required section, with alternative headings) or a list of such lists (several required sections). A document needs one heading of each list (SD305). The comparison ignores case. A value replaces the default of its type. An empty list removes the requirement. The defaults are: decision `["Decision Outcome", "Decision"]`, invariant `["Rules"]`, runbook `["Steps"]`, incident `[["Summary"], ["Root cause"]]`. For a decision, `context` serves the first required section as the summary.

amendment-sections.description: For each type, the names of its amendment sections, in any language. A heading of level 2 or more starts an amendment section if it is a name, or if it starts with a name and a character that is not a letter or a digit. The comparison ignores case. The section continues to the next heading of the same or a higher level. A list replaces the default of its type. The default is `decision = ["Amendments"]`. After a decision is accepted, the text outside its amendment sections is frozen (SD405). For a decision, `context` serves the amendment sections with the outcome.

live-sections.description: For each type, the names of its live sections, such as an implementation status, in any language. They match as amendment sections do. A live section records a current state, so its text can change in place. In a decision, it is not frozen text (no SD405), and new text in it gives no SD605.

history-sections.description: For each type, the names of its history sections (iteration logs, review rounds, superseded notes). They match as amendment sections do. `spec-dna history` moves them, and the amendment sections of a decision, into a reference document. In a decision, a history section is not frozen text.

companion-sections.description: For each type, the names of the sections that belong to the requirements, such as an acceptance map. When `mv` moves requirements, the table rows and list items of these sections that name the moved keys move with them.

enforce-budgets.description: If false, a document over its hard budget gives the warning SD704, never the error SD702. Default true.

lint-severity.description: The rule `lint` of this root (SD801 to SD805), as in 0.1. `rules` has priority over it.

drift-severity.description: The rule `drift` of this root (SD606, SD607), as in 0.1. `rules` has priority over it.

profile.description: The profile of this root, if it differs from the project profile.

rules.description: Severity overrides for this root. They have priority over `[rules]` and over every profile.
Severity overrides. Each key is a rule group (references, ids, budgets, drift, evidence, lint) or a diagnostic code such as `SD702`. A code rule has priority over a group rule. See docs/profiles.md.
